grh_4e7db1c37bc69d6e4364.title: Blossom Otoole
paragraphs: Years after young Claire Barnes ran away when her stern father refused to accept her love for Harry Hall, Dr. Christian learns that the now-elderly Barnes is dying and sends for the daughter he has never stopped missing. Claire returns as Blossom O'Toole, the stage name she adopted after leaving home. She admits to Christian that she and Harry never married and that her hoped-for theatrical success never came; Blossom is only a struggling second-rate actress. She is ashamed to let her father know how little came of the life she chose, but Christian persuades her to see him. At his bedside Claire allows the dying man to believe that she is happy and successful, giving him the comfort and pride he needs in his final moments. The reunion lets father and daughter make peace without forcing Claire to destroy the image that eases his death.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on March 6, 1940. It is listed as episode 70 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Jack Mather, Helen Geddes, and Gloria Holden. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_4e02586b147c09d29a15.title: Blood Relations
paragraphs: Britt returns to the Wilcox ranch to help George Wilcox with a cattle drive and finds George determined to stop his sister Viola from marrying Hunt Coffin simply because Hunt's brother was a criminal. George's efforts escalate from striking Viola to aiming a rifle at Hunt when he comes for her. Viola shoots George in the arm before he can fire and turns his argument about 'bad blood' back on him, then leaves with Hunt. Months later Britt learns the couple married, though George still refuses to reconcile.

grh_4e0d73518a490a9ca334.title: The Rainbow
paragraphs: A dramatization of Wanda Wasilewska's The Rainbow depicts a Ukrainian village under Nazi occupation and the resistance growing around it. Partisan Olena Kostyuk returns while pregnant, is arrested and tortured rather than reveal guerrilla positions, while villagers resist German grain demands and secretly pass military information to the partisans. After the Germans order Olena and her newborn killed, the guerrillas attack the village; the closing image of a rainbow over the fighting is presented as a sign of hope beyond the occupation.

The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.

paragraphs: Englishman Rudolf Rassendyll arrives in Ruritania and, because he is nearly identical to King Rudolf, is forced to impersonate the monarch after the king is drugged and kidnapped by the ambitious Black Michael.
